newsitem.title: UK: Thomson Travel welcomes MMC referral.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Travel welcomes MMC referral.

text.p: Britain's Thomson Travel on Thursday welcomed the decision by the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) to refer the travel industry to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) over allegations of anti-competitive practice.

"We welcome the fact that the MMC will investigate this matter with independence and Thomson is confident that the industry at large, and Thomson in particular, will be vindicated from any allegations of anti-competitive practice," said Paul Brett, chairman and chief executive of Thomson Travel.
"We have been cleared by the OFT before in 1994 and we are sure that we will be cleared again by the MMC," he added.

The MMC will investigate the ownership links between leading tour operators and travel agency chains. It will also look at the practice among travel agents of making the offer of discounted holidays conditional upon the purchase of specific travel insurance.
Thomson, part of Canada's Thomson Corp, is the biggest tour operator and owns the market leading Lunn Poly travel agency.

"We shall argue our case vigorously with the MMC and we are convinced that the facts will bear out our case that the market is competitive and working to the benefit of the consumer," added Thomson's Brett.

John Bridgeman, Director General of Fair Trading, said that the undertakings needed to avoid a reference to the MMC had not been secured despite long discussions with Thomson and Airtours -- the two leading travel companies.
In its statement, Thomson said there were now more high street travel agents than five years ago and the market share of the top five tour operators had declined over the past seven years.
It denied that the consumer was being misled or lost out when insurance was offered as a condition of receiving a discount.
It said the fact that the discount was conditional was widely advertised and its Lunn Poly customers had the alternative of paying the full brochure price and getting the insurance for free.
